ext:bank-santander.after:
Lends to customers in Great Britain and Germany

Partner bank (Santander Consumer Finance) for **GB** and **DE**. Reached at `https://apis.santanderconsumer.com` (test `apis.test.santanderconsumer.com`) through the `cds-finance-engine-scf-client` library, used by [[svc:fae-bank-integration]] (SantanderApiClientFactory). Every call carries a bearer token from Santander's OAuth2 server (`/oauth2provider/oauth2/token`, client credentials, cached until it expires), an `X-IBM-Client-Id` header and an operation id; product and simulation calls also send `Country-Code` and `CallerTransactionID`. We call its multi-simulation API for quotes (v3.8), its checkout route API to submit and update finance applications (configured v2.0; library default v2.5), and its finance-products API (v2.5). Santander also pushes application status back to us (finance assessment status, read by the inbound API); the library holds that payload and maps Santander's statuses to ours. Product type ids per market are fixed in the library: GB loan 2, GB balloon loan 11, DE balloon loan 21, DE financial lease 4.

Previous workspace technology: REST over HTTPS, OAuth2 client credentials plus X-IBM-Client-Id header · ProductsApiClient, RouteApiClient, SimulationApiClient from cds-finance-engine-scf-adapter

ext:bank-zenith.after:
Prices contract hire for business customers in Britain

Leasing partner for **GB** contract hire (Zenith's CHOL quote service, trading as SOL Leasing). Both calls go to one SOAP endpoint, `POST /QuoteService/quoteApi.asmx` on `https://external.solleasing.co.uk` (UAT `external.solleasinguat.co.uk`), with `SOAPAction: http://zenith.co.uk/quoteservice` and an `AuthHeader` (username, password) in the SOAP header: `GetProducts` for contract types and `GetRate` for a quote. Quotes are never saved in Zenith (`quoteaction/complete` is always false). The client is the `cds-finance-engine-zenith-client` library, used only by [[svc:fae-bank-integration]] (ZenithApiClientFactory); SOAP faults are turned into 400/401/500 by known message patterns and counted per car (pno12, sales model, model year). Contract type ids are fixed in the library: GB contract hire is 2 for business and 4 for private customers. There is no application integration.

Previous workspace technology: SOAP 1.2 over HTTPS (Feign SOAPEncoder/JAXB), AuthHeader username and password · ProductsApiClient and QuoteApiClient from cds-finance-engine-zenith-adapter

Not a deployable. README: "This particular repository does not contain any runnable service"; the workflow builds and publishes jars (`cds-paymentservice` 2.0.33-SNAPSHOT) to GitHub Packages. No controllers, Kafka listeners or Dockerfile.

Modules: `cds-paymentservice-shared` (domain model and enums), `-core` (Spring Data MongoDB entities, repositories and services over the shared `payment_services` database, plus validators: a completed transaction cannot be changed, an expired session cannot authorise, an INVOICE session cannot use MANUAL capture), `-properties` (payment accounts, PSP settings, market capabilities and decline-code rules read from Spring Cloud Config under `payments.*`, refreshed by an optional `@Scheduled` job), `-feign` (Feign client builder with Azure AD client-credentials, VCC API key and operation-id interceptors, used by every `*-client` module), `-event-schema` (generates the JSON schema of the recurring-charge event and registers it in Apicurio as `com.volvocars.paymentservice.RecurringChargeEvent`).

Linked by svc:payment-transaction, svc:payment-customer, svc:psp-inbound, svc:psp-integration, svc:payment-scheduler, svc:payment-experience and svc:payment-integration (their pom.xml depend on `cds-paymentservice-*`).

PSPs: the `Psp` enum has one value, STRIPE (source "STRIPE-EXTERNAL"). Trustly appears only as an inbound `Source` (`cds-trustly-inbound`) and in comments.

Payment methods (PaymentMethodType → PaymentOption): CARD → card; LINK, APPLE_PAY, GOOGLE_PAY, PAYPAL → digital wallet; IDEAL, SEPA_DEBIT, DIRECT_BANK_TRANSFER → bank transfer; KLARNA → buy now pay later. REAL_TIME_PAYMENT is an option with no method. All are reached through Stripe.

States: payment session CREATED → ACTIVE → COMPLETED or EXPIRED (sessions expire after 7 days, `payment-session-expiry.json`); session type PAYMENT or INVOICE; capture and authorise AUTOMATIC or MANUAL. Transaction stage = name (START, PROCESS, COMPLETE, TRANSFER, REFUND, CANCEL) × status (SUCCEEDED, PENDING, REQUIRES_AUTHORISE, REQUIRES_CAPTURE, PARTIAL_REFUND, FAILED, CANCELLED, REJECTED), with history; a transaction counts as completed once COMPLETE/SUCCEEDED. PSP status (from Stripe): UNKNOWN, PENDING, PROCESSING, REQUIRES_PAYMENT_METHOD, REQUIRES_CONFIRMATION, REQUIRES_ACTION, REQUIRES_CAPTURE, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, CANCELLED. Refund: PENDING, SUCCEEDED, PARTIAL_REFUND, FAILED (reasons DUPLICATE, FRAUDULENT, REQUESTED_BY_CUSTOMER, OTHER). Transfer to connected accounts: PENDING, SUCCEED, PARTIAL_TRANSFER, FAILED (mode AUTOMATIC by PSP or MANUAL); transfer item and reverse item: PENDING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED; reversal: PENDING, SUCCEED, PARTIAL_REVERSED, FAILED. Payment instrument (saved card): PENDING, ACTIVE, INACTIVE. Recurring-charge retry: ON_SCHEDULE, NEEDS_CARD_UPDATE, WILL_NOT_RETRY, SUCCEEDED, with failure reasons from configurable Stripe decline codes. External event status: PENDING, COMPLETED, REJECTED, CANCELLED, FAILED.

Market capabilities (per market, optionally by product type and sales model): DIRECT_TRANSACTION, AUTO_TRANSFER, CAN_SAVE_CARD, SHOW_PRODUCT_NAME_ON_RECEIPT, RECEIPT_EMAIL. Customers are B2C or B2B; ids may be VOLVO_ID, CRM_ID, ORGANIZATION_CRM_ID, CUSTOMER_ID.

Code owners: @orhanuyaver and @volvo-cars/cd-pop-para.

Previous workspace technology: Java 25 · Maven multi-module libraries (Spring Boot 3, Spring Data MongoDB, Feign, Spring Cloud Config) · published to GitHub Packages

svc:eligibility-cache-worker.after:
Keeps a ready list of who can buy what

Consumes prod.public.productdetailsservice.products and prod.public.manageandsegment.commercialitem (group popcat-eligibility-cache-worker-prod). For a service-plan package or software-option product created or updated in PDS it fetches the matching Manage & Segment items through the Assortment gateway and upserts one document per variant into [[st:eligibility-cache]]; a deleted package or product removes every document of that product. A soft-offer package or software option updated in Manage & Segment rewrites the SKU fields of the documents that point at it. Variants dropped from a product are never removed. Failures are logged and the message is skipped.

Previous workspace classification: job.

sys:cce-glpk-solver.after:
Solves integer linear programmes for car keys

An HTTP wrapper round the GLPK solver, written by Our Studio. [[svc:cce-car-configurator]] sends it a ruleset's constraints with one or more objectives (one per selection or selection group) and reads back one solution per objective. It is reached through puan-sdk-go's `solver.NewClient(GLPK_URL, GLPK_API_KEY, httpClient)`, which posts JSON to `{GLPK_URL}/solve` with an `X-API-KEY` header; any non-200 answer is an error. The HTTP client retries up to 4 times with 200–400 ms linear jitter back-off. Who runs it in dev, QA and production is not in the repo; locally it runs from docker-compose on port 9000. Not the same as [[svc:cce-puan-solver]] (the Python puan-solver-api the car-configuration generator calls).

Our Studio authorship and the local Docker example do not identify who operates the configured dev, QA or production URL. Keep the distinction from the Python PUAN solver.

The operating party, deployment and owning team are not established by the retained caller evidence. This is an unmapped dependency boundary, not a claim of company ownership or a provider implementation.

Previous workspace technology: REST · Our Studio rust-multi-solver-api (image ourstudio/rust-multi-solver-api:glpk-0.1.13, source ourstudio-se/rust-glpk-api) · X-API-KEY header · GLPK_URL

sys:plm-prins.after:
Holds the car specifications from PLM and tells us when they change

The PLM-side specification service for Geely-built cars: Teamcenter (TCPLM) receives specification updates from Geely and pushes them to PRINS, which exposes them as a GraphQL API and calls our webhook on change. Production https://prins-api.prod.volvocars.net/graphql/, QA https://prins-qa-preprod.azurewebsites.net/. We read stored CPV sets, configuration dictionaries and parameters, configuration rules, commercial packages and model-year structure weeks. Every call is retried three times with 2, 4 and 8 seconds between tries, including when the answer carries GraphQL errors.

Previous workspace technology: GraphQL over HTTPS · Authorization AppKey header · Polly retry
